name:        useAnnounce
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Imperatively announces a message to screen readers through a visually-hidden live region. Use it for state that is only conveyed visually; search result counts, "no results", loading and saved confirmations, validation errors (WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages). The polite and assertive regions are created empty on first use and stay mounted, which is what makes announcements reliable: most screen readers ignore a live region that is inserted together with its content. Each message is cleared a couple of seconds after it is announced so stale status does not linger in the accessibility tree. A message is delivered where its caller is: from inside an open Astryx modal it goes to a region inside that modal and is heard there with no change to the calling code; a message sent just as the modal is dismissed is delivered through whatever is exposed afterwards rather than lost. A call made outside the modal, even by the component that renders it, uses the page-body region.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useAnnounce

name:        useInputStatusIcon
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Builds the on-field status affordance for a bordered input and its accessibility wiring, so every input in the family behaves the same for a given status. The attached variant renders a plain glyph and leaves the text to the message box; the detached variant renders nothing here, because the message box already carries its own icon; the tooltip variant renders a real focusable button whose tooltip is reachable by keyboard, pointer, touch and assistive tech. Use it when building a bordered input, not for field-level messaging.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useInputStatusIcon

name:        useCalendarNavigation
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/Calendar
description: Manages visible month state and pagination for calendar components. It provides previous/next month stepping, localized month-year header strings, and pending focus tracking so keyboard arrow navigation seamlessly moves focus across month boundaries into the adjacent month. Use it directly when composing custom calendar headers, pager controls, or dual-month availability pickers.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useCalendarNavigation

name:        useClipboard
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Copy-to-clipboard behavior: the clipboard write, a transient isCopied flag with its own reset timer, and an optional polite screen-reader announcement. Extracted so every copy affordance is a thin control over one implementation instead of re-deriving the timer and announcement. Rapid re-copies restart the reset timer so the confirmation always lasts the full duration, and the timer is cleaned up on unmount. CodeBlock and Timestamp build their built-in copy buttons on it; reach for it directly when building a copy affordance that is not a plain icon button (a menu item, a labeled text button, a copy-on-click value chip).
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useClipboard

name:        useCombobox
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/Selector
description: Tracks the active option of a single-select combobox and handles its keys, while DOM focus stays on the control. It powers Selector and CommandPalette; use it to build a combobox those components do not cover, including one over a single-line text field you render yourself, such as a search field whose results replace a page section, or an "add people" field in a dialog. It renders nothing: you render the field, the listbox and the options, and spread `getFieldProps`, `getListboxProps` and `getOptionProps` onto them, or wire `role`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant` yourself from `onKeyDown` and `getItemId` for a control such as a button.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useCombobox

name:        useHoverCard
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/HoverCard
description: Headless hook for hover-triggered floating cards. Builds on useLayer with hover/focus intent detection, configurable delays, safe hover behavior, and accessible aria-describedby linking. Use for rich previews on hover when you need full control over the trigger or rendered content.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useHoverCard

name:        useIndicatorFocusRing
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Draws the standard focus ring on the indicator of a control whose real input is visually hidden; a checkbox or radio focuses an opacity-0 input, so the ring has to appear on the picture beside it. The ring is painted imperatively on the indicator's own element, which is the only element whose border-radius can shape it, and only on :focus-visible, so pointer clicks stay quiet. Owning it here means a theme-supplied indicator cannot ship a control with no visible focus (WCAG 2.4.7) by ignoring a prop.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useIndicatorFocusRing

name:        useListFocus
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Manages keyboard navigation within a linear list following WAI-ARIA menu/listbox/toolbar patterns. Supports arrow key navigation (vertical, horizontal, or both), Home/End for boundaries, optional wrap-around, RTL, and Escape to close. Opt into hasRovingTabIndex for composite widgets (toolbars, segmented controls, tab strips) that own a single tab stop. Suitable for dropdown menus, toolbars, and any 1D focusable list.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useListFocus

name:        useLongPress
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Detects a single-finger press-and-hold and reports where it happened, so touch users can reach affordances that a pointer gets from right-click. iOS Safari never synthesizes a contextmenu event on long-press, which makes this the only touch route into a cursor-positioned surface such as ContextMenu. The press cancels on movement, lift, multi-touch or unmount. The hold is timed on the touch events' own timestamps: when a busy page handles the lift late, a finger held for the full delay still reports its long press, before the lift acts.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useLongPress

name:        useMenuPress
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: The press model of macOS and iOS menus, for any pointer: the row under the pointer when it is RELEASED is the row that acts, the highlight follows the pointer while it is held, a mouse opens the menu on press and can drag straight into it, and a finger held on the trigger opens it with the finger still down. The pointer is tracked at document level by pointerId, so a finger that slid off the row it landed on is still followed; the click the browser reports at the end of a touch, aimed at the row where the touch began, is swallowed so nothing acts twice. DropdownMenu, ContextMenu, DropdownMenuSubMenu, Selector and the menu bottom sheet already mount it; reach for it directly only when building a menu-like surface of your own.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useMenuPress

name:        useMultiCombobox
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/MultiSelector
description: Tracks the active option of a multi-select combobox and handles its keys, while DOM focus stays on the control. It powers MultiSelector; unlike useCombobox, toggling an option keeps the list open, and rows can carry an action cell. It renders nothing and sets no attributes: the caller renders the control and the list, and wires the ARIA attributes from what it returns.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useMultiCombobox

name:        usePanGesture
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Reports a drag on an element as values, for a surface the product moves itself: a card that follows the finger, a drawer pulled by its handle. A finger, a mouse and a pen all drive it. A mouse or pen drag that starts on selectable text selects that text, and the pan reports nothing. Give that text `user-select: none`. The drag claims its touch at UIKit's 10 pt, as `UIPanGestureRecognizer` does, so a tap stays a tap, and a press or a long press is never reported as a pan. With `axis`, a scroll across that axis that starts on the element stays the page's; without it, the pan takes a drag in any direction, so a finger's scroll that starts on the element moves the element instead of the page. A trackpad scroll still scrolls the page. The hook is a thin layer over `createPanGesture`, the same API for code without React. A drag has no keyboard or assistive-technology path of its own: whatever the drag does needs another way to do it, such as buttons or arrow keys (WCAG 2.5.7). The pan moves nothing itself, so Reduce Motion applies to the motion you drive from it: honor the user's reduced-motion setting in the animation that moves the element. Where a component already offers the behavior, use its prop instead: BottomSheet's `snapPoints`, Carousel's `hasSnap`.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook usePanGesture

name:        usePressFeedback
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: The touch press model every Astryx pressable uses, for a local component that paints its own press. Under a finger, CSS `:active` paints on the touch itself and can outlive the start of a scroll; the press model instead tracks the touch the way UIKit tracks a control: it highlights as the finger lands (after the content-touch delay inside a scroller, where a flick paints nothing), a quick tap answers at the lift, and a scroll that takes the touch cancels it with no fade. One document-level controller does this for every marked element (installed by the first pressable to mount, removed by the last to unmount), so calling the hook adds no listener or state to your element. On a desktop a mouse press is still your `:active` rule: keep it, and drop it under `@media (pointer: coarse)` the way the built-in components do. That query reads the primary pointer, so on a phone or tablet it also drops `:active` for a connected mouse, trackpad or keyboard; the controller paints those presses there (at once, faded at the release), so nothing goes unanswered.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook usePressFeedback

name:        useTableFiltering
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Table plugin that adds inline column filters with popover or inline controls. Pairs with useTableFilterState for managed state. Supports text, select, multi-select, date, and number filter types via PowerSearch field definitions.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useTableFiltering

name:        useTableTreeState
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: State management companion for useTableTreeData. Owns the expanded set (controlled or uncontrolled) and flattens nested data into the visible row array; collapsed subtrees are unmounted, not hidden, so the table body contains exactly the visible rows. Returns expandAll/collapseAll helpers, the aggregate isAllExpanded state (true/false/indeterminate) for a header expand-all control, and a ready-to-use config for the tree plugin. Note: because collapsed rows unmount, cell-local React state inside collapsed subtrees is lost on collapse; lift state that must survive.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useTableTreeState

name:        useTypeahead
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Adds APG type-to-focus search to a collection: printable keystrokes are buffered (resetting after a pause), and the first item whose label starts with the buffer (ignoring case, accents, the stroked letters đ ł ø ħ ŧ ƀ and Turkish ı/İ, the same in every locale; a typed accent prefers the exact match) is reported through onMatch. Pressing the same letter repeatedly cycles through the matches rather than filtering deeper. It moves nothing itself; pair it with the collection's own focus management, most often useListFocus or useGridFocus.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useTypeahead
